# Antagonist Standard Operating Procedure
Your role type decides which rules bind you for the round. You hold a role type [bold]only[/bold] if the game explicitly tells you so - never by inference, never because of what you are carrying, and never because another player says so.
## Crew Aligned / Non-Antagonist
The default. If the game has not told you otherwise, this is you.
Crew-aligned players are expected to work toward a net positive effect on the round. Most players are this most rounds.
## Solo Antagonist
Roles intended to cause problems for the round or for the crew. You are a solo antagonist only where the game clearly and explicitly says so.
Antagonists are exempt from many roleplay rules, [bold]but not all of them[/bold], and never from the core rules.
## Team Antagonist
As a solo antagonist, but with teammates. You are expected [bold]not[/bold] to hinder them, and may be expected to help them.
## Free Agent
Free to act as an antagonist or as crew, and free to change your mind at any point in the round.
Acting as an antagonist binds you to the antagonist standards in this document, Engagement included. Being free to choose is not being free of the rules.
## Familiar
A non-antagonist bound to obey one specific person - the one the game names, and no other.
That obedience holds [bold]even where it breaks roleplay rules or gets you killed[/bold].
## Silicon / Altered Silicon
Bound by their lawset above all else except the core rules.
[bold]Altered Silicon[/bold] is functionally identical; the label marks a lawset that has been hacked, corrupted, or is otherwise non-standard or dangerous.
## Engagement
You are held to the same standard as the crew who hunt you. Play the round out - do not rush people down the moment you are able, and do not open with lethal force where anything short of it would serve.
Rushing is acceptable only where the odds against you are [bold]severely[/bold] unfavourable and there is no other way through.
Everyone else is bound by [textlink="Combat SOP" link="GuideCombatSOP"], which asks them to engage in numbers rather than gun you down the moment they see you. It is not a guarantee of safe passage - there are situations where meeting you with immediate force is the right call - but somebody hunting you down on suspicion alone is not one of them. If you are being denied any room to play at all, [bold]ahelp it[/bold]. Do not carry it into the next shift by treating somebody else the way you were treated.
The room you are given tends to match the room you give. Opening loud - heavy sabotage, bodies in the first minutes, a decisive advantage seized before anyone knows you exist - buys you a shift where nobody has any reason to talk to you first.
## Needless Murderboning
Killing people you had no reason to kill is not fun for anyone, including you. It is over in a minute and it takes the rest of somebody's shift with it.
[bold]Your objectives are the point.[/bold] They are what you are measured against, and almost none of them ask for a body count. A kill that does not move you toward one is just somebody else's round ended for nothing.
## Know How Strong You Are
Pay attention to how much Security and command are actually on shift. When there are few of them - or none - you are not fighting an even shift. You are the single most dangerous thing on the station, with no realistic opposition and nobody able to stop you.
That advantage is not permission. It is the exact situation where you are expected to hold back hardest, because there is nothing left to hold you back.
On a low-population shift, cutting through the crew because you can - killing people who were never a threat to you, who had no way to fight back, and who have nobody coming to help them - is [bold]ahelpable[/bold]. The fact that you were able to do it is not a defence. It is the complaint.
## Illegal Places to Hide or Prepare
Regardless of role type, you may not use the following to hide from the crew or to prepare as an antagonist - lying low, stashing gear or objectives, readying an attack, or holding hostages and prisoners.
- The Shadekin hideout and the Dark, however you got there. - Any planet or map reached by portal that is not Lavaland or an event map in common use.
